Application Materials.content:
- Identification Document: Singapore Citizen: a copy of NRIC; Singapore Permanent Resident: a copy of NRIC AND re-entry permit; Foreigner: a copy of passport personal particulars page.
- Two Referees: Two different referees are required. Please indicate the details of two referees in the online application form, including name, designation and email. The referee will receive a recommendation email from SMU once the JD application is submitted. It may take around 15-20mins to complete the online recommendation form. Where possible, at least one of the recommendations should be from someone who has taught the applicant or supervised applicant's work in university studies. If applicant has left school for a long time and is unable to submit academic references, please provide 2 referees from people who are familiar with applicant's performance, such as employers/colleagues/clients etc. The contents of the recommendation are confidential. Under no circumstance should the applicant be able to see the contents of the recommendation. If referee couldn't receive SMU email with referral link, please ask referee to check spam folders or contact JD programme office at jd@smu.edu.sg directly.
- Degree Certificate: The copy of the degree certificate(s) certified by the issuing institution or a Notary Public/Commissioner of Oath. And the bachelor's degree certificate is compulsory. Combine all degree certificates into one PDF file.
- Transcript: The copy of the official transcript(s) certified by the issuing institution or a Notary Public/Commissioner of Oath. And the undergraduate transcript is compulsory. Combine all official transcript in one PDF file.
- CV: A concise resume that provides chronological information about your educational background, work experiences and accomplishments. Up to two (2) A4 pages.
- Statement of Purpose: All applicants are required to submit a detailed personal statement based on the questions in the online application form. Maximum 600 words to each answer.
- Other Test: GRE/GMAT and SMU Admission Test (SMUAT) is not required to JD programme. LSAT or LNAT is optional.
- Other Supporting Documents: If any additional significant supporting documents, please send them to jd@smu.edu.sg with the applicant’s full name and application reference number by the application deadline. Kindly combine all documents into a single PDF file, with a maximum length of six A4 pages. No additional supporting documents will be accepted after the application deadline.

| **Application Stages (Pre-Acceptance)** | Time |

| Written Test and Interview (Rolling Basis) | December 2025 onwards |
- After written test, shortlisted candidates will be invited for an admission interview conducted by two (2) law faculties.
- The interview will be conducted via Zoom meeting. The JD programme office will contact shortlisted candidates via email to register for interview. Once the registration is confirmed, candidates will receive a confirmation email with azoom link. Reminder emails are available near the interview date.
- After the interview, JD programme office will generally update application outcome via email within 2 weeks.

Application Deadlines.content: The application for 2026 intake is closed.

Academic Requirements.content:
- Non-law and law graduates are welcome to apply for the SMU JD programme if they have **completed an undergraduate education in any discipline with at least a Cum Laude or Second Class Upper Honours degree**; or are **law graduates from a civil law country or a non-gazetted common law university** with **at least a Cum Laude or Second Class Upper Honours degree**.
- Graduating students who will obtain their bachelor's degree by early July of the admission year are welcome to apply using provisional transcript.

GRE GMAT Requirements.content: GRE, GMAT or SMU Admission Test (SMUAT) is not required to the SMU JD application. The LSAT/LNAT is not compulsory to SMU JD.

English Proficiency Requirements.content:
Applicants must show proficiency in the English language. A TOEFL / IELTS test is required if the applicant’s undergraduate degree was not conducted in English. The minimum requirements:
- TOEFL (Paper-based or Internet-based Test): **100**
- IELTS (Academic): **Overall band of 7.5**
From 21 January 2026, TOEFL introduces a new score scale from 1 to 6 in increments of 0.5. The minimum TOEFL score under the new scale as below.
- TOEFL (Paper Based Test or Internet Based Test): **Overall Band of 5**
Apart from above tests, others such as TOEFL Institutional Testing Program (ITP), TOEFL MyBest Scores and Duolingo English Test are not accepted. Scores that are more than **2 years** will not be accepted. More information can be obtained from the [TOEFL website](https://www.ets.org/toefl.html), [IELTS website](https://www.collegeboard.org/) respectively.

Program Overview.content:
The J.D. programme is a **full-time** 3-year programme, comprising 22 courses totaling 25 course units. The curriculum was formulated by legal academics and practitioners after extensive discussions, and endorsed by Singapore Institute of Legal Education and Ministry of Law. The academic year begins in mid-August and follows the same academic calendar/grading scheme as the LL.B programme. **The programme may be accelerated** in some cases for completion within 2 to 2.5 years subject to the approval of the J.D. Committee, which will take into consideration their first term's exam grades.
The J.D. programme bears SMU's distinctives of holistic learning, active seminar-style pedagogy and international and practical exposure. Students engage in a substantial amount of pre-class preparatory reading and thinking, and participate actively in class discussion. Classes are deliberately kept small and a multi-faceted approach to course assessment is adopted, including class participation, term assignments and oral and written presentations. A distinctive feature of the J.D. programme is that lawyers from practice, government and the judiciary will be invited to participate in classroom teaching, providing students with the opportunity to integrate practical expertise with theory and doctrine.
The J.D. programme is a meritorious honours programme. On successful completion, students will be awarded the degree accordingly, depending on their overall performance: J.D. (merit), J.D. (high merit), J.D. cum laude (with distinction), J.D. magna cum laude (with high distinction) or J.D. summa cum laude (with highest distinction). **Students will qualify for legal practice in Singapore (admitted as Advocate and Solicitor of the Supreme Court of Singapore) if they attain a GPA of at least 3.00 in the courses leading to the J.D. degree, and complete the Preparatory Course leading to Part B of the Singapore Bar Examinations conducted by the Singapore Legal Institute of Education, subject to the "Qualified Person" requirements imposed by the Legal Profession (Qualified Persons) Rules.**

Capstone Project: The Law Capstone is designed to prepare students for the future of legal practice. Unlike foundational law courses (for example, Contract and Property) that focus on a narrower range of topics, the Law Capstone helps students look across traditional disciplinary boundaries by working on projects that span multiple areas of the law. Every Law Capstone course will also be an SMU-X course so that the entire cohort of students will be exposed to a healthy degree of experiential learning. SMU-X courses will be taught in even smaller classes (typically 30 and below) with the help of industry mentors.

Financial Aid.content:
The Singapore Management University (SMU) reserves the right to amend the discount schemes for new incoming cohorts when required. Discounts will not be awarded in conjunction with other ongoing discount schemes; discount and scholarship are not stackable. Should a student qualify for more than one discount, only the higher discount amount will be applicable.
- SMU Alumni: S$8,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards). SMU exchange and non-graduating students are not eligible for the alumni discount.
- Singapore Citizens/Permanent Residents Discount: S$5,000 discount off total tuition fees (from 2025 intake onwards).
- ASEAN Nationals Discount: From 2025 intake onwards, a S$3,000 discount off total tuition fees is granted to students from ASEAN nations.
- SkillsFuture: SkillsFuture funding for Singapore Citizens is available; Singapore Citizens aged 40 years and above can claim SkillsFuture Credit (Base Tier) and $4,000 SkillsFuture Credit (Mid-career Tier). This credit is intended to offset out-of-pocket tuition fees, starting from Academic Year 2024/25 intake, commencing on or after 1 May 2024. SkillsFuture Mid-Career Enhanced Subsidy (up to 90% of course fees) is not applied to the SMU JD programme.
- SUTD Alumni Discount (PDPP): With effect from the 2019 admission intake, SUTD alumni who are offered a place in the J.D. programme will be granted a 10% discount under the Pre Experience Postgraduate Degree Experience Programme Agreement (PPDP), spread equally over the 4 payment instalments. The discount is only applicable when they apply within 5 years from graduation from SUTD.
- J.D. Scholarship (For Offered Candidates): Limited scholarships are available for outstanding applicants to the programme. With effect from the 2020 admission intake: First Tier: $10,000; Second Tier: $5,000. The scholarship amount shall be used to offset the programme fees across the four academic terms. Eligibility includes: offered a place in the J.D. Programme; a minimum of second class upper honors/Cum Laude degree qualification or a GPA equivalent; excellent application interview and essay scores; good letters of reference; preference will be given to students who demonstrate financial need. A complete description of the applicant’s financial status, including current savings, stocks, last monthly income as well as any outstanding debts, will be required together with the completed [scholarship application form](https://law.smu.edu.sg/sites/law.smu.edu.sg/files/2023-05/JDscholarshipapplication.pdf), emailed to the Programme Manager.
- J.D. Financial Aid (For J.D. Students): The J.D. Financial Aid is given to J.D. students who face a sudden change in financial circumstances while studying in the programme. Up to $10,000 payable in 4 equal instalments will be used to offset the student’s term course fee across the academic terms. Eligibility: matriculated in the J.D. Programme; minimum CGPA of 3.4 in the J.D. programme; evidence of financial need. Relevant documents together with the completed [scholarship application form](https://law.smu.edu.sg/sites/law.smu.edu.sg/files/2023-05/JDscholarshipapplication.pdf) need to be submitted to the J.D. programme manager.
- Kwa Geok Choo Scholarship (Postgraduate): For J.D. students who have completed at least one year of SMU J.D. studies. Up to 4 postgraduate scholarships will be awarded each year. Each scholarship is tenable for one year, subject to outstanding academic performance and continued observance of the eligibility criteria. Eligibility includes: present full-time SMU Juris Doctor student of any nationality who has completed at least one year of full-time SMU J.D. studies; outstanding academic results (minimum cumulative GPA of 3.7); outstanding leadership qualities; active involvement in co-curricular activities; and demonstrates a spirit of volunteerism. The scholarship has a value of $30,000 and will offer financial support towards tuition fees, living allowances and the purchase of textbooks. No bond is required. Students who meet the CGPA criteria will be sent the application form.
- Course Awards (For J.D. Students): Course awards can be found [here](https://admissions.smu.edu.sg/financial-matters/financial-aid). Students should key in "Juris Doctor" in the search bar to see the awards that JD students are eligible for.
- Wee Chong Jin Top J.D. Graduate Award: Given to the top graduate of the Doctor of Jurisprudence Programme at the Yong Pung How School of Law each year. Each Award has a value of S$6,000.
- Lee Kuan Yew Scholarship: Applicants must be Singapore citizens and will be assessed holistically, including track record of leadership and achievement and potential to excel in their fields/professions. More details and application process can be found [here](https://www.psc.gov.sg/scholarships/postgraduate-scholarships/lee-kuan-yew-scholarship).

Multiple Applications.content: Applicants can apply for **up to three master programmes in a single online form**. Those interested in Juris Doctor (JD) and Master of Laws (LLM) may apply for both together. If an applicant is also applying for other programmes in the same application form, they should follow the requirements specified for those additional programmes.

Deferral Admission Policy.content: Apply during the year you wish to enrol as **there is no deferred admission for the JD programme**.

Conditional Admission Policy.content:
- Graduating students who will obtain their bachelor's degree by **early July of the admission year** are welcome to apply using provisional transcript.
- Candidates who do not meet the academic criteria but intend to sit for the Bar Exam and practice law in Singapore may consider the SMU [Master of Laws (LLM) programme](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm) first; they may subsequently be granted direct entry to SMU JD subject to the [transferring requirements](https://law.smu.edu.sg/llm/admissions/transfer-smu-jd).
